name: Greece (since 1830)
summary: The modern Greek state, independent from the Ottoman Empire in 1830, which grew to its present borders by 1947 and has been a republic since 1974.

knownFor.label: Revival of the Olympic Games
knownFor.note: The first modern Olympics were held in Athens.

location.value: Mostly on the Balkan peninsula of south-east Europe, with thousands of islands.

terrain.value: Mostly mountainous, with long coasts and many islands.

climate.value: Mediterranean, with hot, dry summers and mild, wetter winters; mountains are cooler and snowy.
climate.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

resources.value: Olives, shipping, tourism, marble and bauxite.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

disasters.value: Earthquakes and wildfires, such as the deadly Mati fire of 2018.
disasters.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

urbanisation.value: Athens is the largest city, followed by Thessaloniki and Patras.

disease.value: Good public health, though health spending was cut sharply during the 2010s debt crisis.
disease.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

migration.value: The 1923 population exchange with Turkey (Treaty of Lausanne); about 1.5 million Greek refugees had to be resettled.

economicBase.value: Shipping and tourism are major sectors (the ninth most-visited country in 2024); also farming.

tradeRoutes.value: One of the world’s largest merchant fleets.
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

wealth.value: A high-income economy, though much smaller since the debt crisis that began in 2009.
wealth.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

inequality.value: Unemployment and poverty rose sharply after 2009, especially among young people.
inequality.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

governmentType.value: A parliamentary republic since the transition to democracy in 1974; earlier a kingdom.

keyRulers.value: Eleftherios Venizelos, the Cretan politician called to power after the 1909 coup.

succession.value: After the junta (1967–74), a referendum in 1974 abolished the monarchy and made Greece a republic.
succession.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

institutions.value: The Hellenic Parliament, a president as head of state, and an independent judiciary.
institutions.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

stability.value: Occupation in the Second World War, the Greek Civil War and instability, leading to a military dictatorship (1967–74).

eliteConflict.value: Rivalry between royalists and republicans, and between left and right, caused a civil war (1946–49) and later a junta.
eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

armyAndTech.value: A NATO member since 1952 with a large army for its size, partly because of tension with Turkey.
armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

majorWars.value: The War of Independence (from 1821) and the Balkan Wars (1912–13); the war with Turkey ended with the Treaty of Lausanne (1923).

territoryChange.value: Grew from a small state to today’s borders by 1947.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

alliancesRivals.value: Joined NATO (1952); the tenth member of what is now the EU (1981).

inventions.value: Few major modern inventions; Greece’s influence is mostly through ancient heritage and shipping.
inventions.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

scienceEducation.value: Free public schooling and universities, with high rates of university attendance.
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

openness.value: Open to trade and the EU, which Greece joined in 1981 and the euro in 2001.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

communicationTransport.value: Ferries link the many islands, and the Athens metro and new motorways have modernised transport.
communicationTransport.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

religion.value: Greek Orthodox Christianity, which helped shape modern Greek identity.

languageWriting.value: Modern Greek, written in the Greek alphabet.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

artsArchitecture.value: Poetry by Cavafy and Seferis (Nobel 1963), music such as rebetiko, and the Acropolis in Athens.
artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

socialStructure.value: A large middle class, strong family ties, and many self-employed people.
socialStructure.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

sharedIdentity.value: Strong link to ancient and Byzantine heritage.
sharedIdentity.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

dailyLife.value: Whitewashed houses and apartments; olive oil, feta, fish.
dailyLife.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

ideasReligions.value: The ideas of ancient democracy and the Orthodox Church shaped national identity.
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

colonisation.value: Greece was never a colonial power; it grew to its present size by absorbing Ottoman and Italian territory.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

riseSignals.value: Independence after a long war that began in 1821.

peakPeriod.value: Rapid growth in the 1950s–60s, after the civil war.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

declineSignals.value: The Great Recession and the eurozone crisis from 2010.

outcome.value: Greece continues as an independent republic.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

sources.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence

overallCertainty.source: Wikipedia: Greece; Wikipedia: Greek War of Independence
